title: Rav Yitzchak bar Ashyan
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: Hyman says he was a student of R' Huna. In Sukkah 42a: Rav Shmuel bar Chatai said that Rav Hamnuna Saba said that Rav Yitzchak bar Ashyin said that Rav Huna said in the name of Rav; likewise in Gittin 39a. Yuchasin writes that he was a student of Rav, and Hyman understands him to refer to Pesachim 45b: R' Yitzchak bar Ashi said in the name of Rav; Dikdukei Soferim reads bar Ashyan said in the name of Rav. Likewise in Yevamot 108b he said, “And Rav concedes that she is permitted to his brother.”

Hyman says that his statements have remained with us through his student Rav Idi bar Avin. In Berakhot 14a, Rav Idi bar Avin said in the name of R' Yitzchak bar Ashyan: “A person may not attend to his personal business before praying, as it is said—”; whoever prays and then sets out on a journey, the Holy One, blessed be He, attends to his needs. In Ketubot 27a he said in his name, “If there is one hiding place, it protects all the priests’ wives.” In Chullin 33a: “One who wishes to become healthy,” etc.; there, 105a: first waters (washing before a meal) are a mitzvah, and last waters (washing afterward) are obligatory; there, 106: handwashing for non-sacred food, because of a safeguard for terumah. In Bekhorot 38b: “Adar and Nisan—moist [produce],” etc.
